source_read: PMC HTML (PMC8111570, author manuscript; N Engl J Med 2021;384:140-153): abstract, introduction, Methods (design, oversight, participants, outcomes, statistics), Results (participants with Table 1, primary outcome with Table 2, secondary outcomes, safety with Table 3 and footnotes), Discussion, acknowledgments/funding/disclosures. Figures 1-2 are images (legends read). Protocol, SAP and Supplementary Appendix PDFs not opened. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03078075: study details (design, arms, eligibility, outcomes, locations, dates, documents list) and posted results (participant flow, primary outcome counts, all-cause mortality, serious adverse events by arm).

claims.overstatement: None material. Points the wording does not carry: the response is a short-window outcome (3 of 4 negative samples in weeks 5-6 or 11-12), the 11.1-point effect is a design-weighted (0.43/0.57) combination of a stage-1 comparison and a stage-2 comparison among placebo non-responders, not a simple 12-week between-group difference; the authors give NNT 9 'under the assumptions in this trial'; participants had to be opioid-free and not in other treatment, and adherence and retention were high, which the authors say may limit generalizability; an interim analysis by the DSMB showed a significant difference and led to a sample-size increase without adjustment of the significance level.
claims.note: Editors' calculation: weighted responses reproduce exactly (0.43 x 16.5% + 0.57 x 11.4% = 13.6%; 0.43 x 3.4% + 0.57 x 1.8% = 2.5%; difference 11.1). With SE derived from the printed Wald z (11.1/4.53 = 2.45) the two-sided 95% CI is 6.3 to 15.9, matching the paper's printed lower boundary of 6.3; using the rounded SE of 2.5 gives 6.2 to 16.0, so the claim's 'about 6.2 to 16.0' is acceptable but 6.3-15.9 is more exact. NNT 1/0.111 = 9 (range about 6 to 16 across the CI). Equal-weight sensitivity: 11.4 (6.5-16.2); complete-case: 18.7 (11.6-25.8). Registry results reproduce the stage-wise counts (18/109 vs 10/294; 13/114 vs 2/111) and show no deaths in any arm.

anchors.locator: Methods > Trial design and conduct; Participants; Table 1
anchors.extracted: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, sequential parallel comparison design at 8 US sites (May 2017-July 2019). 403 adults with DSM-5 moderate/severe methamphetamine use disorder, use on >=18 of 30 days (mean 26.7), >=2 positive urines, opioid-free, not in concurrent treatment; stage 1 randomization 0.26:0.74 (109 vs 294); 225 placebo non-responders re-randomized 1:1 in stage 2 (114 vs 111). Study conditions: injectable extended-release naltrexone every 3 weeks plus daily oral extended-release bupropion, or matching placebos.

Response (>=3 of 4 methamphetamine-negative urines in last 2 weeks of a stage): stage 1 18/109 (16.5%) vs 10/294 (3.4%); stage 2 13/114 (11.4%) vs 2/111 (1.8%). Weighted 13.6% vs 2.5%; difference 11.1 +/- 2.5 (SE) percentage points; lower boundary of 95% CI 6.3; Wald z 4.53; P<0.001 (one-sided test at 0.025).
Weights 0.43 (stage 1) and 0.57 (stage 2) chosen to maximize power; ITT with missing urines counted as non-response. Authors: NNT 9 under the trial's assumptions.
Prespecified sensitivity analyses: complete cases 18.7 points (11.6-25.8); equal stage weights 11.4 points (6.5-16.2).

Nausea 37.6% vs 15.3% (stage 1) and 28.1% vs 7.2% (stage 2); vomiting 11.9% vs 2.0% and 10.5% vs 2.7%; also constipation, dry mouth, dizziness, tremor, hyperhidrosis, malaise, decreased appetite more frequent in stage 1; headache less frequent (11.9% vs 23.1%). Participants with >=1 serious adverse event: 1 (0.9%) vs 4 (1.4%), P=1.00 (stage 1); 3 (2.6%) vs 4 (3.6%), P=0.72 (stage 2). Registry: no deaths in any arm.

Limitations stated by authors: low attrition and high adherence may limit generalizability; few women; oral ingestion not observed; SPCD hard to interpret; DSMB interim analysis showed a significant difference and sample size was raised from 370 to 400 without adjusting the significance level; 12-week duration.

key_findings.correction: The paper calls 6.3 the 'lower boundary of the 95% confidence interval'; it equals 11.1 - 1.96 x 2.45 (SE from the printed Wald z, 11.1/4.53), i.e. the lower limit of a two-sided 95% CI (one-sided 97.5%, matching the one-sided alpha of 0.025), not a one-sided 95% bound (which would be about 7.1). Two-sided 95% CI 6.3 to 15.9 with the z-derived SE (6.2 to 16.0 only with the rounded SE of 2.5). Also: the NNT sentence is in Discussion, 2nd paragraph, not 3rd.
Figures confirmed; the statement that oral ingestion was not observed is in Discussion, 3rd paragraph (the Discussion has four paragraphs; the 4th is the one-sentence conclusion).

Confirmed for the paper. The registry's posted SAE table differs: 16 SAEs (7 on naltrexone-bupropion, 9 on placebo), no 'homicidal ideation' event, and 7 naltrexone-bupropion participants with an SAE (1 + 3 re-randomized + 3 not re-randomized).
Minor: a PHQ-9 mean of 19.9 sits at the boundary of 'moderately severe' (15-19) and 'severe' (20-27) per the registry's own banding.
Content confirmed; the interim-analysis/no-alpha-adjustment statement is in Discussion, 3rd paragraph (Methods > Statistical analysis, 1st paragraph is correct).
Registry study start is 2017-05-05 (paper: 23 May 2017); registration on 2 March 2017 is prospective either way.

reporting_issues.note: Found independently. The registry supports 7 participants (1 stage 1; 3 stage 2 re-randomized; 3 not re-randomized) on naltrexone-bupropion with an SAE.

Found independently. The registry places appendicitis in stage 2 (non-re-randomized placebo), contradicting the footnote's 'before randomization', and supports the main text's 13 + 4 split (registry total 16, without homicidal ideation).
A reading limitation rather than a reporting issue of the paper.

The paper prints only the lower boundary of 'the 95% confidence interval' (6.3), which is the two-sided 95% lower limit, not a one-sided bound; the unprinted upper limit is 15.9 from the z-derived SE (16.0 from the rounded SE).
Registry: TES = percentage of expected urine screens negative; paper: TEA = 4-item self-report.
Figure 2 legend mentions visits at weeks 13 and 16.

missed: Registry vs paper discrepancies not on the card: (a) posted SAE table lists 16 events (7 naltrexone-bupropion, 9 placebo) with no homicidal-ideation SAE, and appendicitis in stage 2 non-re-randomized placebo; (b) registry sites include UTHealth Houston (CNRA) and one Dallas site, whereas the paper's acknowledgments name two Dallas sites and no Houston; (c) registry describes twice-weekly 'observed oral medication dosing', while the paper says oral ingestion was not observed; (d) the SAP copy posted on the registry is dated 2019-09-13, after primary completion (2019-07-03), although the 0.26:0.74 SPCD randomization shows the weighted design was planned from the start.

Registry posted results show that stage-1 naltrexone-bupropion participants (not re-randomized) had 21/109 (19.3%) responders at weeks 11-12, and non-re-randomized placebo participants 9/69 (13.0%); these are outside the SPCD primary analysis but describe continued-treatment response, not reported in the paper.
